input.quote: Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
input.rationale: Section 9 provides only for-cause (9.1), insolvency (9.2), security/service-level (9.3) and force-majeure (27.3) exits; there is no Customer right to terminate for convenience, and the term runs three years (8.1) with Section 2.1 expressly locking Customer into a take-or-pay commitment "without reduction or termination rights." That is walk-away territory under the rule (no Customer convenience right in a multi-year term) and fails even the fallback (60–90 days' notice with a capped fee). Vendor likewise has no convenience right, which is consistent with our position, so the redline only adds a 30-day Customer convenience right with a pro-rata refund and carves it out of Section 2.1 so the new right is effective.

proposal.summary: Add Customer termination for convenience on 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund; carve out from take-or-pay lock-in
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have added a Customer right to terminate for convenience on 30 days' notice with a refund of prepaid Fees, and carved that right out of Section 2.1, because our playbook does not permit a three-year commitment with no exit. If helpful, we can move to 60 days' notice as a fallback.

ops.text: Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, without penalty, early-termination charge, or other liability, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid Fees for the period after the effective date of termination. Vendor has no right to terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience during a term.

ops.oldText: on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
ops.newText: on a take-or-pay basis, subject to Customer's termination rights under this Agreement, including Section 9.4.
